{"id": "63dea25f-60b7-4cc4-9321-0012798afbf2", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — disabling your own VPC Flow Logs or turning off S3 data event logging in CloudTrail won't reduce your GuardDuty bill.

**Why:** GuardDuty doesn't read your account's own log configurations. It consumes these data sources through its own independent, duplicate stream directly from the AWS backend — separate from whatever VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, or S3 data event settings you have configured. As AWS documentation puts it:

> "Your individual service log configuration or filtering rules (for VPC Flow Logs, DNS Logs, CloudTrail Events, S3 Data Events, Kubernetes Audit Logs, and Lambda Network Logs) do not impact the logs/events processed by GuardDuty."

So turning those off just removes logs from *your* account (and any cost you pay for storing/processing them separately) — it has zero effect on what GuardDuty ingests or bills for, since GuardDuty pulls its own copy regardless.

**One real cost lever that does exist:** if you're using GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring on EC2/EKS with an active runtime agent, GuardDuty skips VPC Flow Log processing charges for that instance while the agent is actively sending data — but that's tied to Runtime Monitoring status, not your own flow log settings.

If you're looking to actually reduce GuardDuty spend, the right levers are things like adjusting which optional protection plans (S3 Protection, EKS Protection, Lambda Protection, RDS Protection, etc.) are enabled, not your own logging configuration.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
